scenes.title: A quiet beginning
scenes.subtitle: Hi, Nidhi… hold my hand whenever you're ready, and we'll walk through our story.
scenes.text: Hey, Nidhi. I made this to say I'm sorry and to remember our story. You can pause, skip, or leave whenever you want. You don't have to answer anything.
scenes.alt: A dark theater stage where a warm spotlight clicks on, the narrator drops in from above, slowly stands up looking at Nidhi, waves hi, and reaches his hand toward the bottom-right corner.

scenes.title: Before we really noticed each other
scenes.subtitle: From sleepy online classes to joking on the Class Seven and Eight back benches, I was lost in my own world.
scenes.text: We were classmates before we became close. During online school, I barely paid attention. When school resumed and we were moving through Class Seven and Class Eight, I was usually joking with my friends at the back.
scenes.alt: First a sleepy morning online class on a laptop, then a sunlit Class Seven and Eight classroom with back benches and a drifting paper airplane.

scenes.title: The paper house
scenes.subtitle: I wired the series and parallel circuit houses—and you sent me a picture of the tiny paper sofa and bed you painted.
scenes.text: Our science group had to build little houses to show series and parallel circuits. I worked on the electrical part. You made tiny paper furniture, including a sofa and bed, painted it, and sent me a picture on Messenger. That was your first direct message to me.

scenes.title: Across the rooftops
scenes.subtitle: Playing guitar on my rooftop within sight of your balcony—you sent a snap of the song, and I sent one back.
scenes.text: Your balcony could be seen from my rooftop. One day I was there with my cousins, playing guitar and singing. You asked someone we knew if that was my home, then sent me a snap of the song. I sent one back. It was a small, shy beginning.

scenes.title: Our own little language
scenes.subtitle: Power-cut evenings matching steps across our rooftops, daily messages, coaching walks, silly jokes, and skipping class for food.
scenes.text: The messages grew into good mornings, good nights, and long talks. When the electricity went out, we sometimes met each other's eyes from the rooftop and balcony and matched steps. We went to coaching together, teased each other, and shared ordinary details all day.

scenes.title: The river and our very detailed plan
scenes.subtitle: Our minute-by-minute river boat outing at sunset, paying that surprise overcharge quietly, and the silent rickshaw ride back.
scenes.text: I planned our outing almost minute by minute: a boat on the nearby river and time to watch the sunset before coaching. We were still friends, not calling it a date. When we got off the boat, the renter demanded much more money than we expected. We paid and left. In the rickshaw back, we mostly looked at each other and let the silence do the talking.

scenes.title: Best friends, before we had the words
scenes.subtitle: Acting like a 'love teacher' though I'd never been in love—secretly wishing that when you said someone would love me, you meant yourself.
scenes.text: For months, your good-morning message was often the first thing I looked for. I used to explain love like I was some kind of love teacher, even though I had never been in love. Whenever you said someone would love me, a quiet part of me wished you meant yourself.

scenes.title: The silence, and finding our way back
scenes.dateLabel: Two quiet days; exact date unknown
scenes.subtitle: I thought people misunderstood our closeness and created distance—leaving two quiet days when I should have spoken honestly.
scenes.text: I believed people were misunderstanding our friendship, so I decided we should make distance. I stopped talking properly, then told you we should end that closeness. We barely messaged for two days. I should have explained myself with more care.
scenes.alt: Two still windows across a quiet dusk street as two silent days pass.

scenes.title: The chocolate wrapper
scenes.subtitle: I sent you a snap of the chocolate wrapper I had kept and framed—and we came back to how we were, as best friends.
scenes.text: I had kept the wrapper from a chocolate you gave me, framed it, and sent you a snap. You asked if we could get back to how we were. We started messaging again and found our friendship.

scenes.title: The night our feelings had words
scenes.dateLabel: November 2023; after November 10; exact day unknown
scenes.subtitle: Sometime in November 2023, after my birthday on November 10, on an ordinary night call, the words finally came: 'I love you.'
scenes.text: Sometime in November 2023, after my birthday, we were on a regular night call. We both seemed to know what the other wanted to say. Then the words finally came: “I love you.” We never chose one exact anniversary.

scenes.title: All the little chapters after that
scenes.subtitle: All the little chapters since—messages, letters, calls, jokes, and these frames waiting for our real pictures.
scenes.text: Our years together are not only the big scenes. They are the messages, photos, letters, calls, jokes, and small things we remembered for each other. I want to add only the memories that feel good and true for both of us.
scenes.alt: An open two-page handmade memory book spread displaying six photo and letter frames ready for real personal pictures.

scenes.title: What I am sorry for now
scenes.subtitle: Recently I said we should break up and said 'I don't love you anymore'—those were my words, nothing excuses that hurt, and I am sorry.
scenes.text: Recently, I said we should break up, and I said, “I don't love you anymore.” Those were my words. Whatever was happening inside me does not excuse the hurt or uncertainty they caused. I am sorry I spoke to you that way.
scenes.alt: A quiet pool of warm light where the narrator stands with honest accountability, plus an optional playful foam-helmet cartoon bonk.

optionalInteraction.title: A tiny cartoon bonk?
optionalInteraction.copy: Optional playful cartoon bonk—never replaces the apology.
optionalInteraction.reaction: BONK! A silly foam-helmet wobble—the real hurt still matters, and I'm listening.

scenes.title: What changes after this
scenes.subtitle: Pause when upset, speak without threatening us, listen when I hurt you, and respect the space or time you ask for.
scenes.text: I want to pause before speaking when I'm upset, explain my feelings without threatening the relationship, listen when you say I have hurt you, and respect the time or space you ask for. A promise in a game is only a sentence. The change has to happen after the game is closed.
commitments: Listen when I have hurt you
Respect the space or time you ask for

scenes.title: An open ending
scenes.subtitle: I'm sorry, Nidhi. Thank you for every chapter—you owe me no forgiveness, answer, or decision, and I will respect whatever you need.
scenes.text: I'm sorry, Nidhi. Thank you for being part of so many chapters of my life. You do not owe me forgiveness, an answer, or a decision because I made this. You can leave here whenever you want. Whatever you need next, I will respect it.
scenes.alt: Warm golden morning light where the narrator gently offers a blooming flower with no obligation or expectation of a reply.
